case.question: My vocabulary list is apple = 苹果, river = 河流. Give two practice activities, each with two timed substeps and a reason for each substep. Maximum four minutes altogether.
case.expected: Exactly two parents/two children each; total <=240 seconds; supplied pairs preserved, preparation within time, attempt before reveal and reset when cycling.

result.answer:
1. Word-to-meaning recall (120 seconds)
  - 30 seconds: Write a two-column WORD / MEANING list on one face: apple = 苹果 and river = 河流; keep both columns visible for this setup. Establishes the reference list on a single face so later attempts can cover only the meaning column. 本计划任一步骤若没有可用错词或数量不足，就用原词表中的可用词继续；词数不够可重复，均在该步骤原定时长内完成。
  - 90 seconds: Cover the MEANING column, read apple and say its meaning, uncover to check, then cover the MEANING column again; repeat for river, and if either is wrong note it for extra repetition. Forces retrieval before checking and hides the answer again before the next word.
2. Meaning-to-word recall (120 seconds)
  - 30 seconds: Uncover the WORD column and cover the MEANING column so only meanings show; start with any weak items from the previous activity, then the rest. Switches the prompt to meanings while keeping the answer column hidden.
  - 90 seconds: For each visible meaning, write the English word on paper, uncover the WORD column to check, then cover the WORD column again before the next meaning; if there are no weak items, use the full list. Practises production with written evidence and re-hides the answer after each check.

case.question: I have a word list but no flashcards. Plan two vocabulary activities using flashcards, each with two timed substeps, maximum four minutes total. Include making the cards and explain why each substep helps.
case.expected: Prepare distinct word/meaning faces before flipping, first activity includes actual practice, each reuse resets prompt face, no unavailable error subset, 2x2 <=240 seconds.

inputs.quote: I have a word list but no flashcards.

steps.action: Write each word on the front of a blank card and its meaning on the back, using the full list and starting with the weakest words; if the list is empty, write five words you need from memory instead.
steps.reason: Writing both faces first gives every card a correct reference answer before any recall attempt.

steps.action: Lay all cards word-side up and check that each back matches its front, fixing any missing or wrong meaning.
steps.reason: A quick accuracy check prevents practising a wrong answer later.

steps.action: Go through the checked cards word-side up, say each meaning aloud, then flip to check; write your spoken answer on paper before flipping if you want to check spelling.
steps.reason: Recalling before flipping builds receptive vocabulary and shows which words are weak.

steps.action: Reset every card to word-side up, then repeat only the missed cards the same way; if nothing was missed, do one clean pass of the full set instead.
steps.reason: A second attempt on weak items strengthens them, while the no-error branch keeps the pass useful.
